---
title: "Fewer Coefficients: Why We Need Less Data, Not More"
description: "A dashboard that plots everything behaves like a polynomial forced through every point."
date: 2026-10-02
categories: [essay, data]
---

We keep producing more data, only for it to end up in dashboards. That's not what we need.

Fit a polynomial of degree $n-1$ through $n$ points and it hits every one of them, yet swings wildly in between (Runge's phenomenon). A low-order fit

$$
\hat f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{p} a_k x^k, \qquad p \ll n,
$$

captures the *shape* and predicts where we haven't measured.

A useful test: **does this output change a decision?** If a dashboard tile never alters what anyone does, it's a coefficient that isn't pulling its weight.

*Full working paper: [Show What Changed, Not the Data](../2026-09-29-show-what-changed/index.qmd).*
